values.note: $15 a night per single site (2 vehicles per site), charged May 1 - September 28, 2026; free camping in the off-season, snow dependent. Pay by cash or check.

fees.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/lolo/recreation/bitterroot-flat-campground ('Fees until 9/28/2026, open to free camping in off-season, snow dependent', 'Single Site: $15 per night (2 vehicle limit per site)', 'Fee charged May 1, 2026- September 28, 2026', 'Please be prepared to pay with CASH or CHECK'; page last updated September 15, 2026), read 2026-10-22

values.note: Drinking water from a hand pump. Picnic tables and fire rings. No horses or pack animals.

facilities.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/lolo/recreation/bitterroot-flat-campground ('Restrooms: Flush toilet(s)', 'Yes, drinking water is available from a hand pump', 'Horse/Pack animals are not allowed at this site'), read 2026-10-22

values.note: 'Open year-round, snow dependent.' Fees charged early May to late September; free in the off-season.
Not on recreation.gov and the Forest Service page gives no reservation channel (only the generic line 'Sites may be reservable and reservation fees apply').

note: Lolo NF (Missoula RD), beside Rock Creek, a blue-ribbon trout stream, ~23 mi up Rock Creek Rd (#102) from I-90 exit 126, among ponderosa pine and Douglas-fir. Max trailer ~32 ft, but the last ~11 mi of Rock Creek Rd is rough, narrow and single-lane, and the Forest Service says trailers, motorhomes and tow vehicles are not recommended. --Claude
summary: Forest Service (Lolo NF, Missoula RD), first-come (not on recreation.gov). Confirmed $15 (2026; free off-season, so fees now 0/15), 50% senior/access discount. Changed toilets vault -> flush (FS page 'Flush toilet(s)'); added hand-pump drinking water, open year-round (snow dependent). Not stated: site count, max rig length. No current alert names Rock Creek Rd. Note trimmed.
flags: Criteria: the Forest Service page says 'Trailers, motorhomes and tow vehicles not recommended due to the narrow and rough road' (Rock Creek Road #102) and 'Large RVs not recommended.'
